title: Taiwan's Egis and France's SiPearl Join Forces on a New Chip
summaryZh: 神盾集團與法國SiPearl結盟，共同開發小晶片CPU Mobius100。
summaryHi: ताइवान की Egis और फ्रांस की SiPearl मिलकर नया चिपलेट CPU बनाएँगी।
summaryEs: La taiwanesa Egis y la francesa SiPearl se alían para crear un nuevo procesador.
summaryJa: 台湾の神盾と仏SiPearlが提携、チップレットCPUを共同開発へ。
summaryKo: 대만 이지스와 프랑스 SiPearl, 칩렛 CPU 공동 개발 제휴.
summaryEn: Taiwan's Egis and France's SiPearl team up to develop a new chiplet CPU.
paragraphs: Taiwanese chip designer Egis Group has formed a strategic partnership with French processor developer SiPearl, signing cooperation and investment agreements at a technology event in Taipei on Thursday. The deal covers the joint development of a new central processing unit, the Mobius100, and an expansion into markets across Europe, the Middle East and Africa.

Under the arrangement, Egis will contribute its chip technology, while SiPearl will supply expertise in software and system design. Egis is also joining SiPearl's latest funding round, although the size of its investment was not revealed.

SiPearl, which describes itself as Europe's only designer of high-performance CPUs, already has a first-generation chip, Rhea1, manufactured by TSMC. The processor powers part of Germany's JUPITER supercomputer. Chief executive Philippe Notton said the Mobius100 platform would form the basis of its second-generation chip, Rhea2, shortening development time.

The Mobius100 relies on chiplets, smaller chips combined in a single package. According to Egis, this approach allows designers to mix manufacturing processes and reuse components, cutting the cost of redesigns as advanced chip development grows more expensive.

The partners aim to produce samples by the end of 2027 and begin mass production in the second half of 2028, depending on testing and customer demand. Economics Minister Kung Ming-hsin attended the ceremony.
A Taiwanese chip company and a French chip company will work together. The Taiwanese group is called Egis. The French company is called SiPearl. They signed an agreement in Taipei on Thursday.
The two companies will make a new computer chip together. Its name is Mobius100. It is a CPU, the main brain of a computer.
Egis will give its chip technology. SiPearl will help with software. Egis will also put money into SiPearl.
SiPearl says it is the only company in Europe that designs very strong computer brains. Its first chip is already in a big German supercomputer. The Taiwanese company TSMC makes this chip.
The new chip is made from small parts called chiplets. This can save time and money. The companies hope to make many new chips in 2028.

Egis Group, a Taiwanese chip design company, has signed a partnership with SiPearl, a French company that designs computer processors. The two firms signed the agreements in Taipei on Thursday, and Egis will also invest in SiPearl. They did not say how much money.

Together they will develop a central processing unit (CPU) called Mobius100. Egis will provide the chip technology, while SiPearl will bring its knowledge of software and computer systems. The partners also plan to sell their products in Europe, the Middle East and Africa.

SiPearl says it is Europe's only designer of high-performance CPUs. Its first chip, Rhea1, is made by TSMC and is used in JUPITER, a powerful supercomputer in Germany. SiPearl will use the Mobius100 design for its next chip, Rhea2, which will save development time.

Mobius100 is built from chiplets, small chips that work together like building blocks. A manager at Egis explained that designers can reuse parts, which lowers costs as advanced chips become more expensive to develop.
The companies hope to have samples by the end of 2027 and start mass production in the second half of 2028. Taiwan's economics minister attended the signing.

Taiwanese chip designer Egis Group has formed a strategic partnership with French processor developer SiPearl, signing cooperation and investment agreements at a technology event in Taipei on Thursday. The deal covers the joint development of a new central processing unit, the Mobius100, and an expansion into markets across Europe, the Middle East and Africa.

Under the arrangement, Egis will contribute its chip technology, while SiPearl will supply expertise in software and system design. Egis is also joining SiPearl's latest funding round, although the size of its investment was not revealed.

SiPearl, which describes itself as Europe's only designer of high-performance CPUs, already has a first-generation chip, Rhea1, manufactured by TSMC. The processor powers part of Germany's JUPITER supercomputer. Chief executive Philippe Notton said the Mobius100 platform would form the basis of its second-generation chip, Rhea2, shortening development time.

The Mobius100 relies on chiplets, smaller chips combined in a single package. According to Egis, this approach allows designers to mix manufacturing processes and reuse components, cutting the cost of redesigns as advanced chip development grows more expensive.

The partners aim to produce samples by the end of 2027 and begin mass production in the second half of 2028, depending on testing and customer demand. Economics Minister Kung Ming-hsin attended the ceremony.

Egis Group, a Taiwanese chip design company, has struck a strategic alliance with SiPearl, the French firm that bills itself as Europe's sole designer of high-performance processors. Agreements on cooperation and investment were signed at the group's Tech Day in Taipei on Thursday, in the presence of senior Taiwanese officials and France's representative in Taipei.

At the heart of the partnership is the Mobius100, a central processing unit the two companies will co-develop. Egis, through its subsidiary Alcor Micro, will provide the underlying chip technology, whereas SiPearl will contribute its software and systems know-how. The alliance is also intended to give Egis a foothold in Europe, the Middle East and Africa.

SiPearl is no newcomer. Its first-generation Rhea1 processor, fabricated by TSMC, already sits inside the CPU cluster of JUPITER, Germany's flagship supercomputer. Chief executive Philippe Notton said building its successor, Rhea2, on the Mobius100 platform would significantly compress development timelines.

The design is based on chiplets, modular dies assembled into one package. Proponents argue that this allows engineers to combine different manufacturing processes and recycle proven components, sparing them costly redesigns at a time when cutting-edge chips are becoming ever more expensive to produce. Even so, Egis acknowledged that packaging, software and verification remain demanding.

Egis has also joined SiPearl's Series B funding round, though the amount was undisclosed. The companies are targeting samples by late 2027 and volume production in the second half of 2028, subject to validation.

In a move that strengthens technological ties between Taiwan and Europe, Taiwanese chip design group Egis has entered a strategic partnership with SiPearl, a French developer of high-performance processors. The two companies signed cooperation and investment agreements in Taipei on Thursday, an event attended by Taiwan's economics minister and a deputy foreign minister.

The collaboration centres on the Mobius100, a central processing unit to be developed jointly. Each partner brings complementary strengths: Egis contributes semiconductor technology, while SiPearl offers expertise in software and system integration. Furthermore, the agreement is expected to facilitate the expansion of Egis into Europe, the Middle East and Africa.

SiPearl claims to be the only European company designing high-performance CPUs. Its first processor, Rhea1, which is manufactured by TSMC, is already deployed in Germany's JUPITER supercomputer. The firm intends to base its second-generation chip on the Mobius100 platform, thereby reducing development time considerably.

A significant feature of the design is its use of chiplets, small modular chips combined within a single package. This approach enables engineers to integrate different manufacturing processes and reuse existing components, which substantially lowers redesign costs. Nevertheless, packaging and system verification remain considerable challenges.
Egis is also participating in SiPearl's latest funding round, although the sum has not been disclosed. Mass production is scheduled for the second half of 2028, provided the chip passes validation.
